# Nihilo Solutions

> Nihilo Solutions is a small firm in Connecticut that builds custom operational
> automations for growing companies. We take repeating operational work off a team
> and turn it into a system that runs without them: recurring reports, meter and
> usage readings, client and record lookups, exception review, and the movement of
> the same record between tools. Engagements are scoped to one workflow at a time,
> priced fixed in writing, and handed over on completion. We work across the
> Northeast and take remote engagements nationwide.

## What we build

Types of systems, not a product catalog. Every build is scoped to the client's
process, their existing tools, and their definition of done.

- **Operational service reporting**. Weekly or monthly packs that today live in a
  spreadsheet, a shared drive, or someone's head. We connect the sources, apply the
  same rules every time, and deliver the report in the format the team already uses.
  Covers service, ticket and job summaries, exception and overdue lists, and
  scheduled delivery to email or a shared folder.
- **Meter and usage reading**. Any operation that still depends on a person reading
  a device, a portal, or a print-out and typing the number in. We capture the
  reading, validate it, and write it to the system that already bills or tracks
  usage. Fewer estimated reads and fewer corrections later.
- **Client and record lookup**. A lookup built against the systems a client already
  has, so the right customer, job, or account comes back in one step instead of a
  search across three tools. Covers account lookup, job or ticket retrieval during
  a call, and less re-keying between dispatch, billing, and support.
- **Similar operational workflows**. Where the pattern is repeatable, rules-based,
  and currently done by a person: intake, status updates, data movement between
  tools, scheduled checks, exception flagging instead of full-list review.

## How we work

Four steps. A 30-minute discovery call on one concrete workflow, free, with a
straight answer on fit. A written process map and a fixed-price scope stating what
will be automated, what will not, and what is needed from the client. A build
against the client's live data and tools, reviewed early. Then review beside the
current process, adjust, and hand off.

What we need from a client: a real process owner who can walk us through last
week's run, access to the source the data already lives in, and a specific
definition of done.

## How we are different

- Custom operational automation, not app-to-app zaps. We build where the work is
  messy: a spreadsheet plus a portal plus a meter plus a report that has to look a
  certain way.
- No new platform required first. We build against the tools and files a client
  already uses. Required infrastructure is in the scope before work starts.
- Fixed scope and a fixed price, in writing, before the build. Not hours against an
  open retainer unless ongoing support is requested after handoff.
- The client owns the workflow when we are done, and their team is shown how to run
  it and how to change a rule when the business changes.
- The people who scope the work stay on it through handoff. No account managers.
- AI is used only where it earns its place: reading a meter image, matching a messy
  client name, drafting a summary. Much of the value is reliable plumbing: pull,
  validate, write, notify.
- We publish no invented case studies, client names, or performance metrics.

## Who this is for

Operations, service, dispatch, billing, and office teams that still do the same
work by hand every week, with data already living in sheets, portals, meters, or a
few disconnected tools, and a willingness to start with one workflow rather than a
company-wide rebuild.

Not a fit: a generic website chatbot, a full ERP or platform replacement, a process
nobody can describe, work that is different every time with no rules, or a staffed
marketing agency engagement.
